correctness.rationale: Contractive IFS gives digit series and unique invariant law; conditional expectation of |X-1/2| yields lower bound with exact strict quadratic penalty. Order-preserving r-contractive quantile recursion gives Q(u)<=u for u<1/2 and symmetric reverse for u>1/2, saturating the KR dual potential. Pointwise distance-to-attractor lower bound and nearest-point projection yield a unique supported optimizer; gap-length square series gives its exact cost and endpoint atoms. The first deleted-gap endpoint r has positive projected mass but can only be reached from endpoint 1, whose projected mass is zero, excluding any stationary state-dependent switch. All boundaries r in (0,1/2), p in [0,1] checked, no finite test used as universal proof.

value.rationale: The result supplies a sharp numerical and structural feasibility benchmark for a recent inverse invariant-measure design question: fair iid sampling is uniquely optimal with a quadratic margin, yet the optimal measure on the same physical attractor is unique, atomic and dynamically unrealizable under arbitrary state-dependent selection. The exact relative penalty diverges as the separation gap vanishes, although absolute costs vanish; this illustrates a genuinely nonuniform implementability limit. Not a general theorem for arbitrary IFS.
